message.content: {"B_expression":"-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)","C_expression":"-1/2","derivation":"Retain the active parent program. B(r) = -1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2) is the source exact-root quotient: substituting into g = r/2 + r^2*B(r) with u=0 gives g = r/(1+sqrt(1+r)) = sqrt(1+r)-1, so (1+g)^2 = 1+r = p identically. It is C-infinity on r > -1, an open neighborhood containing the full evaluation rectangle |r| < 1/2. C = -1/2 cancels the leading O(ur) cross term in E = 2(1+u)g + g^2 - r: the O(ur) coefficient is 1 + 2C = 0. Numerical feedback from the parent stage confirms residuals at or below ~2e-71 (machine epsilon) for every in-support point (|r| <= 1/4, |u| <= 1/8), across UNIFORM, LEFT, and BOTH families. The single r = -1 row has |r| > 1/2, so chi_r = 0 and only the linear g = r/2 applies, yielding the expected uncorrected residual 0.25. No algebraic error term is visible above roundoff; the remaining higher-order terms O(ur^2), O(u^2 r), O(r^3) are all at or below 1e-20 for the observed state magnitudes. Smoothness: sqrt(1+r) > 0 for r > -1, no poles, no branch points, no max/clips; C is a constant. Both bodies are C-infinity on an open neighborhood of the closed outer rectangle.","inspect":[],"note":"Program retained unchanged from P03_W0. All in-support residuals are at machine precision; no visible algebraic error. A successor should verify that the next-stage targets (p1 = p0 + tau^2*k1, p2 = p1 + tau^3*k2) produce r values still within |r| <= 1/4 at the in-support points, so chi_r remains 1 and the quadratic correction continues to apply. If a future stage pushes |r| above 1/4, the chi_r ramp will attenuate the correction smoothly; no discontinuity is expected. The extreme z values (z = -15, 17, -3, 5, etc.) in LEFT/RIGHT/BOTH rows have |u| >> 1/4, so chi_u = 0 and only the linear r/2 applies; this is by design and not a failure. The r = -1 LEFT row is permanently outside chi_r support. No analytic-domain certificate is claimed; smoothness follows from the explicit algebraic form (rational in sqrt(1+r), constant C) on r > -1. This is a local coefficient-field construction for the fixed two-slot covariance quotient; it does not establish global NS admissibility or any PDE estimate."}
